bullets: Futures bounce (S&P +0.4%, Nasdaq +0.9%) after last week's ~$5T AI-driven tech rout; Semis -17% and Tech -10% remain the week's biggest sector laggards.
VIX up 13% to 19.4 and 10Y yield near 4.93% show lingering caution even as futures turn green; Brent oil fell 3% to $110.
Geopolitical overhang: Rubio says US and Iran both prepare for strikes despite talk of a peaceful end; US midterm elections due Nov 3.
Data-heavy week: ISM Manufacturing today, JOLTS Wed, ISM Services Wed, and Friday's jobs report (NFP, unemployment rate) could move swing positions mid-hold.

AVTR.why: Q3 beat and FY guidance raised, but stock fell on margin headwinds, European weakness, and a soft 0.75-1.25% organic growth guide; Barclays cut to Underweight (PT $16) the same week - AVTR-specific caution, not sector news.
AVTR.bull: Profit swung positive, revenue beat, FY guidance raised, leverage falling despite the post-earnings dip.
AVTR.bear: Barclays went Underweight; margins still pressured by Europe/pricing and organic growth guide is only 0.75-1.25%.
AVTR.catalysts: none found (next: Dec 8 Investor Day, outside hold window)

NTAP.why: Dropped with a broad AI-hardware selloff after weak Intel/Amazon-linked results hit Nasdaq tech (sector data: Tech -10%, Semis -17% over the period); no NTAP-specific downgrade, only a neutral Guggenheim initiation.
NTAP.bull: Drop tracks a sector-wide tech selloff, not NTAP fundamentals; ratings skew buy-heavy (8 buy, 0 sell).
NTAP.bear: A technical 'sell signal' and in-focus headlines suggest momentum turned, with no fresh bullish catalyst to force a quick bounce.

CTSH.why: Q3 revenue/EPS beat, but bookings fell 7% y/y, Health Sciences and P&R segments shrank, and Q4 guide implies deceleration; EPS gain came entirely from buybacks, not operations - company-specific demand softening, not a sector move.
CTSH.bull: Headline EPS/revenue beat, new OpenAI/AI partnership wins, and Guggenheim raised PT to $80 (Buy).
CTSH.bear: Bookings fell 7%, two core segments shrank, and EPS growth came entirely from buybacks, not real demand.

WEX.why: Beat Q3 and raised guidance, yet fell on cash-quality concerns and Morgan Stanley doubting WEX can sustain 5-10% 2027 organic growth after benefits/corporate-payments revenue trailed estimates; no rating downgrades, both UBS and MS raised price targets.
WEX.bull: Q3 beat, guidance raised, margins expanded to 14% from 10.8%, and UBS/Morgan Stanley both hiked price targets.
WEX.bear: Morgan Stanley doubts 2027 organic growth holds after benefits/corporate-payments trailed estimates, and cash-quality of earnings is questioned.
